args.focus: {"claude": "post-commitment continuation: traces that already stated an answer inside the thinking but kept deliberating until the cap (17 of 53 truncated bank traces). Find what the model predicts right after its first in-think answer statement in finished vs truncated traces (token log-probs, top-k), and which components push toward reopening the question (\"But\", \"Wait\", \"Alternatively\") instead of confirming and closing.", "ed_a": "hedging episodes: \"maybe\" / \"perhaps\" / \"Alternatively\" are 2-3x denser in truncated traces than in finished ones. Find the components (MLP neurons, heads, residual directions) active at the onset of such reconsideration episodes, test whether they fire on points already settled earlier in the trace, and whether damping them shortens the specific wasteful episodes without hurting finished answers."}

{"claude": "decision formation in truncated traces that never reach an answer: in finished traces, find the point where the model first commits to an option and what precedes it (which options were eliminated, what evidence was stated); in truncated traces of similar questions, find what is missing at the corresponding point. Look for components that mark \"enough evidence to decide\" or that keep an option open, and test whether strengthening the decision signal makes those traces commit to a correct answer (not just stop).", "ed_a": "revisiting settled options: truncated traces deliberate option by option and often return to options they already ruled out or evaluated. Measure how often an option is re-evaluated after an explicit verdict on it, find the components active when the model reopens an option it already judged (heads attending back to the earlier verdict, MLP neurons), and test whether damping them saves tokens without reducing accuracy on finished traces."}
